Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 23 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Enhanced Southwest Monsoon (Habagat)
Issued at: 2:00 PM, 24 September 2025(Wednesday)

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Zambales and Bataan.
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, expect light to moderate rains over Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Metro Manila, Rizal, Laguna and Quezon within the next 3 hours.
Light to moderate with occasional heavy rains affecting Pampanga, Bulacan, Cavite and Batangas(Nasugbu, Lian, Tuy, Calatagan, Balayan) which may persist within 3 hours and may affect nearby areas.

The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 5:00 PM today.
For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZJq1n.

#MSNews | The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority urged the pople to reduce, reuse, and recycle in order to minimize waste and prevent clogging of waterways, which can cause flooding in the metropolis. 

Residents are also being urged to take part in the Recyclables Mo, Palit Grocery project, where they earn points by submitting recyclable materials, which can then be exchanged for grocery products.

The MMDA Mobile Materials Recovery Facility operations continue in various barangays in Metro Manila, aiming to promote waste segregation and recycling. 

In the latest operations conducted in Barangay Rosario, Pasig City, a total of 143 kilograms of recyclables were gathered; in Barangay 813, Manila, 377 kilograms of recyclables were collected; Barangay Alabang in Muntinlupa City recorded the highest amount, with 732 kilograms of recyclables, while Barangays 178 and 179 in Pasay City recorded a collection of 439.5 kilograms of recyclables. | via Joel Zurbano 

📷 MMDA

For more news updates, visit https://t.co/rmQCnNSOvI.

UERM BACKS FILIPINOS’ CALL VS CORRUPTION

University of the East Ramon Magsaysay Memorial Medical Center (UERM) on Wednesday, Sept. 24, said it stands in solidarity with Filipinos in their call for truth and justice, stressing its commitment to integrity, transparency and accountability.

UERM President and Chief Academic Officer Dr. Norbert Lingling D. Uy said corruption is a “disease” that hinders the nation’s rightful progress and prosperity.

“We envision a nation founded on honesty and respect… The future we envision for our country is one we must build together, united in purpose,” Uy said.

UERM, located in Sta. Mesa, Manila, has also been known to experience occasional flooding during heavy rains. The issue has become a pressing concern nationwide amid alleged corruption in flood control projects, including “ghost” works and overpriced contracts flagged in Senate hearings.
